items.title: Hundreds of holidaymakers in limbo as travel company cancels trips
items.description: Australian travellers say they have been dumped days and weeks before their overseas holidays after a tour company cancelled their trips.

items.title: Treasurer says 'death tax' claims are a scare campaign, 'pure and simple'
items.description: The Coalition seizes on the federal government's broken tax promises, claiming a "death tax" has been sneaked into changes to trusts passed on through inheritance. The treasurer says that is a scare campaign.

items.title: Live: Albanese rejects claim discretionary trust plan amounts to 'death tax'
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has rejected suggestion the government's planned tax on discretionary trusts amounts to a so-called "death tax". Follow live.

items.title: Power rationed, medical supplies in doubt as fuel crisis lingers for millions
items.description: It has been more than two months since the US and Israel launched strikes in Iran. But the impact of the conflict continues globally.

items.title: Church warns 'everything's on the table' as redress bill continues to climb
items.description: Tasmania's Anglican Church says what it expects to pay in compensation to victim-survivors of child sexual abuse has more than doubled in the past three years.

items.title: Inside the deadly search to recover four divers' bodies from a deep-sea Maldives cave
items.description: Expert divers have been sent to the Maldives to retrieve four bodies in a deep-sea cave network, in a search mission that's already killed one military rescue diver.

items.title: A Canberra woman's husband said not to book return flights. It was a case of exit trafficking
items.description: Advocates for migrant women say they're seeing more cases of exit trafficking, a little-known crime involving coercion, threats or deception to organise a person's departure from Australia.

items.title: Federal government intervenes for third time over China-linked stakes in rare earths miner
items.description: The federal treasurer orders another six companies to divest their holdings in Northern Minerals as concerns grow in Canberra that Chinese-backed investors are trying to seize control of the rare earths mining company.

items.title: Taiwan president responds after Trump's visit to China
items.description: Speaking after Donald Trump's meeting with China's president, Taiwan's leader says the island will not be sacrificed or traded and will not give up its free way of life.

items.title: Live: ASX down after Wall Street losses, AUD also lower, oil rises
items.description: The ASX 200 has opened the new trading week with a fall of 1.45 per cent, continuing its downward trend during the month of May. Meanwhile, uncertainty over the Iran war has seen Brent crude oil rise above $110 a barrel. Follow live.

items.title: 'Boomer bashing': Are cuts to private health rebates addressing generational or wealth inequality?
items.description: The federal government plans to reduce private health insurance rebates for older Australians, a move one advocate fears could "tip many over the edge".

items.title: For the second straight game, Slater has overlooked Walsh. But why?
items.description: Reece Walsh's generational run to end 2025 was almost without peer, but he has rejoined the ranks of the mortals to start this year.

items.title: Horror MotoGP crash leaves rider with broken neck
items.description: Alex Márquez is lucky to be alive after he spectacularly wrecked his MotoGP bike during the Catalan Grand Prix in Barcelona, while Johann Zarco was also taken to hospital after an equally terrifying crash later in the race.

items.title: Stronger mouse poison allowed for 'worst plague on record'
items.description: Farm groups have welcomed the chemical regulator's long-awaited decision to approve double-strength mouse baits amid plague numbers in Western Australia and South Australia.

items.title: Want to eat more beans? Try these easy and delicious recipes
items.description: From vegetarian chilli to hearty soup, these easy recipes might convince you to add beans to your regular dinner rotation.

items.title: Meet the women rangers in Central Australia working to protect country
items.description: Dozens of Central Land Council Aboriginal rangers gathered east of Alice Springs last week for the 2026 Women's Ranger Camp — a time for health, learning and healing in the wake of the town's recent loss of Kumanjayi Little Baby.

items.title: How an Australian designer's fashion fame spurred a mental health unravelling
items.description: Rochelle Gregory has clothed everyone from Paris Hilton to Dua Lipa. Now the designer is using film to candidly explore her mental health battle while showcasing her latest collection.

items.title: Alice Springs' gruelling West Macs Monster ultra-marathon, in pictures
items.description: Over distances of up to 231km, 573 runners took to the Larapinta Trail outside Alice Springs at the weekend to compete in the 2026 West Macs Monster.

items.title: Why the US, UK and NZ haven't raised interest rates in years
items.description: As Australians pay more on their mortgages, some countries have had no rise in their interest rate in recent years. So what's going on?

items.title: Liberal senator speaks out against Taylor's budget reply
items.description: Senator Andrew McLachlan raises concerns over Angus Taylor's use of the term "mass immigration" and plan to push tax-paying migrants off welfare benefits.

items.title: Qld developer donation overhaul yields $170,000 in cash
items.description: More than $170,000 in donations from developers has been given to Queensland state politicians since laws banning developer donations were overturned in March.

items.title: Breaking: Anglo American sells central Qld coal mines to UK company
items.description: Anglo American says it has sold its five steelmaking coal mines in central Queensland to a UK mining company Dhilmar Ltd for up to $5.43 billion.

items.title: Trial begins for concert pianist suing Melbourne Symphony Orchestra
items.description: Pianist Jayson Gillham is suing the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra in the Federal Court over political discrimination after comments he made on stage during a 2024 performance.

items.title: Some NT cases could halt if landmark legal challenge succeeds
items.description: Lawyers in the Northern Territory are commencing a landmark legal challenge that could require courts to halt some cases due to defendants being unable to access a lawyer amid a worsening legal aid crisis.

items.title: 'This is the end': SA health chief recalls terrifying moment she was hit by car
items.description: SA public health chief Nicola Spurrier opens up about the moment when she was knocked from her bike by a car last year, and recounted the experience — which left her with broken bones and fearing for her life — only hours after a 39-year-old motorcyclist was killed in a crash in the Adelaide Hills.
